title: A Hurricane Releases a Nuclear Bomb's Energy Every 20 Minutes

scenes.text: A hurricane releases the energy of a nuclear bomb every 20 minutes.
A 10 megaton bomb. Every 20 minutes. All day. For days.
Almost all of that is heat. Water evaporates from warm ocean, rises, and dumps its energy as it turns back into rain.
The winds you see are less than 10 percent of it.
One hurricane puts out five times more power than all of humanity uses.
So no, you can't nuke a hurricane. The hurricane is already the bomb.

description:
A mature hurricane releases heat energy equivalent to a 10-megaton nuclear bomb exploding every 20 minutes, according to NOAA's Hurricane Research Division.
Most of that energy is heat released as water vapour condenses into rain; the winds account for less than 10 percent. The total, 50 to 200 trillion watts, is several times humanity's entire energy use. That is also why the old idea of nuking a hurricane would not work.
Have you ever been through a hurricane? Comment below.
first_comment: In the 1950s a US government meteorologist seriously proposed detonating a bomb inside a hurricane's eye to weaken it. NOAA's answer: the fallout would ride the trade winds, and the storm would barely notice. What's the wildest weather you've lived through?
